_doc: Proposed new findings for findings/audit/zz-structural.json: second writers of a store that no ontology Root/Scope line, ADR or product store plan names (class 'undeclared' in st-check-own-census) and that no existing finding covers. Covered second writers reuse F-0404 (restore's adjacency and degree-cache writes), F-0618 (ledger node delete, legacy vector tables), F-1604 (sample API updateProtein), F-1801 (restore over the ledger), F-1805 (restore over temporal aggregates), F-1806 (Snapshot.ImportGlobals / SetNodeJSON load any global). Every record here is from source (disposition confirmed-source); none was run live.

findings.title: ^KG("prop") has no owning module, and four modules write it
findings.intended: Playbook §3.4 (experiment/playbook-uplift/verification-playbook.txt:32, 311): each store has a single write owner. ADJ-0 lists the stores the adjacency module owns (experiment/playbook-uplift/ontology/04-adjacency.md:49) and ^KG("prop") is not among them. No other Root or Scope line names it. GraphStores.Inventory lists it as graph content (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/GraphStores.cls:82).
findings.observed: st-check-own-census: writers of ^KG("prop") are Graph.KG.TraversalBuild.BuildKG (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/TraversalBuild.cls:65, Kill ^KG("prop")), the 4.0.0 node-store step rekey_kg_node_stores (iris_vector_graph/migrations/kg_node_stores.py:176), Graph.KG.Eraser (EraseGraph :239, EraseIdSet :579, EraseAll :794, ForgetNodes :1327) and the restore paths (snapshot STORE_PLAN; Snapshot.ImportGlobals/SetNodeJSON, conditional). Readers include Graph.KG.Subgraph.
findings.remedy: Name an owner for ^KG("prop") (the adjacency module's ADJ-0 list, or a module of its own) and route the other writers through it, or retire the store if nothing current needs it.
findings.notes: Structural: no wrong answer was shown. The store is erased and archived like owned content (GraphStores, STORE_PLAN).

findings.title: Dropping a neighborhood_vector index handle kills ^NKG("q") in the interned snapshot
findings.intended: ^NKG is owned by the adjacency module (04-adjacency.md:49, ADJ-0 'Stores owned ... ^NKG') with the algorithms module (10-algorithms.md:5-9); VEC owns its own index globals (06-vectors.md:8-9). Playbook §3.4: single write owner.
findings.observed: iris_vector_graph/_engine/vector.py:329-330 VectorMixin._neighborhood_index_drop runs Native API kill('^NKG', 'q') for any index name; index_protocol.py:50 routes the drop of a 'neighborhood_vector' index handle to it. The build and search of that index type are not implemented (vector.py:322-328 raise NotImplementedError). No other product site writes ^NKG("q") except Graph.KG.GraphIndex.DropNKG (Kill ^NKG) and the restore paths (st-check-own-census).
findings.remedy: Give the neighborhood index a global of its own (or make the drop a no-op while the index type is unimplemented); never kill a sub-store of ^NKG from the vector module.
findings.notes: Only the 'q' subtree is killed and nothing else writes it today, so no current answer changes; the write is a latent cross-module hazard.

findings.title: A Cypher DELETE deletes vector rows and reification rows itself, and only from the legacy vector table
findings.intended: The vector tables are VEC's (06-vectors.md:5-8: the routed kg_emb_<hash> tables and the three legacy tables), reifications are INT's (15-integrations.md:5-10: reify_edge, get_reifications, delete_reification). The Cypher module's Scope names writes of the graph tables (08-cypher-sql.md:5, CYP-D1 :40: nodes, rdf_labels, rdf_props, rdf_edges). Playbook §3.4: single write owner.
findings.observed: iris_vector_graph/cypher/translator.py translate_delete_clause adds DELETE statements on Graph_KG.kg_NodeEmbeddings (:10750 for reifier nodes, :10783 for deleted nodes) and on Graph_KG.rdf_reifications (:10757, :10796, :10800) to the write transaction (st-check-own-census sites). No statement names a routed kg_emb_/kg_eemb_ table.
findings.remedy: Delete a node's vectors and reification links through the owners' paths (the eraser's route-aware node erase, delete_reification), so every route is reached and one module keeps each store's rules.
findings.notes: Not run here. Routed node tables carry a foreign key onto nodes (iris_vector_graph/_engine/schema.py:255-263, fk_{short}), so a DETACH DELETE of a node holding a routed vector may be refused whole or leave the vector, as F-0618 shows for the ledger's node delete; a live check would decide.

findings.title: Graph.KG.ArnoAccel.BumpVersion moves the adjacency module's graph-version token
findings.intended: The graph-version token ^KG("__version") is in the adjacency module's owned stores (04-adjacency.md:49 ADJ-0; :64 ADJ-D15 'Each write that can change an answer moves it up'); ADR-0011 puts every rule that must hold on each adjacency write in Graph.KG.Adjacency (docs/adr/0011-the-adjacency-index-has-one-writer-module.md:12-30). Playbook §3.4: single write owner.
findings.observed: iris_src/src/Graph/KG/ArnoAccel.cls:295-302 BumpVersion runs $Increment(^KG("__version")) and $Increment(^NKG("$meta","version")) outside Graph.KG.Adjacency (st-check-own-census: the only undeclared writer of ^KG("__version") besides the restore's _raise_kg_version, snapshot.py:57, covered by F-0404).
findings.remedy: Bump the token through the adjacency module (one method that also keeps the degree generation rules), and name the Arno bridge as its caller.
findings.notes: An extra increment only invalidates caches; no wrong answer follows from this write alone.

findings.title: EraseAll kills ^ArnoKG, a store the erase plan (GraphStores.Inventory) does not list
findings.intended: Graph.KG.GraphStores.Inventory is the product's list of the stores erasure covers (12-erasure.md:5 Scope; iris_src/src/Graph/KG/GraphStores.cls:28-130, 'Stated once here rather than rediscovered by each consumer'). ^ArnoKG belongs to the algorithms module's Arno bridge (10-algorithms.md:5-8). Playbook §3.4: single write owner.
findings.observed: iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Eraser.cls:806 (EraseAll) runs Kill ^ArnoKG; GraphStores.Inventory has no ^ArnoKG entry; EraseGraph and EraseNodes write no ^ArnoKG (st-check-own-census).
findings.remedy: List ^ArnoKG in GraphStores.Inventory (with the scope it can be erased by) and clear it through the Arno bridge's own invalidation (NKGAccelLoader.InvalidateAdjCache).
findings.notes: The kill itself is the right effect for an erase-all (ADR-0004). Not checked here: whether a graph erasure (which does not touch ^ArnoKG) leaves an Arno-path answer built from the erased graph's cached adjacency; that is an erasure-completeness question for the owning lanes.

findings.title: The FHIR graph build writes the adjacency label index and the vector and document rows itself
findings.intended: ^KG("label") is the adjacency module's (03-writes.md:43 WRT-D7 'owned by the adjacency module'; 04-adjacency.md:49), written by Graph.KG.Adjacency.PutLabel/RemoveLabel, which move the graph-version token; the label functional index calls them on each rdf_labels row (iris_vector_graph/schema.py:780, iris_src/src/Graph/KG/LabelIndex.cls:10-27). Vector and document rows are VEC's (06-vectors.md:5-8; 07-text-search.md:9-10). INT-F1.17 (15-integrations.md:94) says that with the functional index declared the row writes keep ^KG and the class skips its own Put/Remove.
findings.observed: iris_src/src/Graph/KG/FHIRGraph.cls sets ^KG("label",...) directly in SyncProps (:2566, unconditionally) and EnsureNode (:2616, unconditionally) and kills it in SyncProps (:2560) and DropNode (:2475-2477, :2491) when not indexed; DropNode deletes Graph_KG.docs, kg_NodeEmbeddings, kg_NodeEmbeddings_optimized and every routed node table (:2481-2489) and DeleteEdge deletes kg_EdgeEmbeddings and every routed edge table (:2588-2594) by its own SQL (st-check-own-census).
findings.remedy: Write labels only through the rows (indexed) or Graph.KG.Adjacency.PutLabel/RemoveLabel (not indexed), and delete a node's vectors and documents through the eraser's node path, so each store keeps one writer and the version token moves.
findings.notes: Consequence not demonstrated: in an indexed namespace the direct Set duplicates the hook's write; where the label index is not declared, label changes made here do not move ^KG("__version"), so a cached algorithm answer could outlive them (the F-0405 family). Confidence medium for that reason.

findings.title: The SQL adapter's node delete removes document and reification rows by its own SQL
findings.intended: OPS-B5.6 (17-operations.md:189): delete nodes removes ids 'with their labels, properties, edges and vectors' (no documents or reification links named). Documents are VEC's (07-text-search.md:9-10), reifications INT's (15-integrations.md:5-10). Playbook §3.4: single write owner.
findings.observed: iris_vector_graph/stores/iris_sql_store.py _delete_nodes_sql deletes Graph_KG.rdf_reifications rows (:1387) and Graph_KG.docs rows (:1403) itself, besides the content and legacy vector tables OPS-B5.6 names (st-check-own-census).
findings.remedy: Delete through the owners (the eraser's node erase, which already reaches documents and routes) and state in OPS-B5.6 what the delete removes.
findings.notes: The SQL path is the fallback when the erasure server code is absent (OPS-T5.6.1, 17-operations.md:190).
